story.headline: Texas steamrolls Georgia, 37-14
body: Texas dominated from start to finish in a 37-14 rout over Georgia in Week 1 PCFL action, with Arch Manning earning Player of the Game honors after going for 21 of 35 for 252 yards and 3 TDs.
The Longhorns outgained Georgia 482–190 in total offense, including 245 yards on the ground. Georgia never got the offense going, managing 190 total yards on the night.
Up next, Texas hosts Ohio State in Week 2.

aiStory.headline: Manning throws three touchdowns as Texas rolls Georgia 37-14
aiStory.dek: Texas opens the season 1-0 and atop the Eastern Atlantic while Georgia falls to 0-1 in the Eastern Southern.
body: Fourth quarter, 2:14 remaining, Texas ball at the Georgia 19, leading 34-14. Arch Manning's pass on third down is knocked down by Malaki Starks, bringing up fourth and four. Will Stone steps in and drills a 36-yard field goal, pushing the margin to 23 and sealing a 37-14 victory.

Georgia struck first when TJ Giles found Colbie Young on a 37-yard touchdown pass at 3:21 of the opening quarter for a 7-3 lead. Texas answered with a one-yard Manning-to-Xavier Worthy strike early in the second, then marched 89 yards capped by Quintrevion Wisner's 14-yard touchdown run for a 17-7 halftime edge. Manning hit Worthy again from two yards out to open the third, and after Georgia's Giles connected with Jimmy Campbell on an eight-yard score, Manning found Wisner on a one-yard pass early in the fourth. Stone added field goals from 45 and 36 yards to close the scoring.

Texas dominated the lines of scrimmage, outgaining Georgia 482 yards to 190 and rushing for 245 against 58. The Longhorns converted 55 percent of third downs while holding the Bulldogs to 17 percent, and a 35:58 to 24:02 time-of-possession advantage wore Georgia down. Manning finished 21 of 35 for 252 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions, Jerrick Gibson led the league in rushing with 128 yards on 15 carries, and Ryan Wingo added six catches for 80 yards. Georgia's offense managed just eight first downs and went 1-for-4 on fourth down in the final period.

Texas moves to 1-0, claims the top spot in the power poll and leads the Eastern Atlantic with a W1 streak. Georgia drops to 0-1, falls to tenth in the poll and sits last in the Eastern Southern on a L1 skid. Next week Texas hosts Ohio State (1-0) while Georgia travels to Colorado (0-1).
aiStory.turningPoint: Texas took the lead for good on Manning's one-yard touchdown pass to Xavier Worthy at 13:28 of the second quarter, capping a 73-yard drive that made it 10-7.
byTheNumbers: Texas rushed for 245 yards to Georgia's 58, a 187-yard edge that fueled a 35:58 possession advantage.
The Longhorns converted 6 of 11 third downs (55%) while the Bulldogs managed just 2 of 12 (17%).
Georgia went 1-for-4 on fourth down, all failures coming in the fourth quarter with the game out of reach.
Jerrick Gibson's 128 rushing yards lead the PCFL after Week 1, averaging 8.5 yards per carry.

unsungHero.name: Will Stone
unsungHero.why: Made all three field-goal attempts, including a 45-yarder and the clinching 36-yarder, providing nine points without a miss.

aiStory.headline: Nussmeier, LSU ground game wear down Miami in fourth quarter
aiStory.dek: LSU opens the season 1-0 and atop the Eastern Southern while Miami falls to 0-1 with a road test at Washington looming.
body: With 2:24 left in the fourth quarter, LSU faced second and goal at the Miami 2; Garrett Nussmeier handed to Rico McNeil, who punched in a 2-yard touchdown and Lilian Munoz added the extra point to make it 38-27, the largest lead of the night at 11 points.

Miami struck first when Graham Mertz hit Gunner Benton for a 16-yard touchdown and a successful two-point try put the Hurricanes up 8-0 at 11:45 of the first quarter; Nussmeier answered with a 14-yard keeper and a two-point conversion to knot it at 8. A Vencie Sites field goal and a Romeo Dixon 2-yard run pushed Miami ahead 18-8 before Nussmeier found Paul Barnhardt for a 15-yard score to cut the gap to 18-15. A safety on a Nussmeier sack sent Miami into halftime leading 20-15. LSU opened the third quarter with a 75-yard drive capped by a 20-yard Nussmeier-to-Woody Hasty strike for a 21-20 lead, then a 39-yard Munoz field goal made it 24-20. Mertz hit Colby Lilly for a 14-yard touchdown to reclaim a 27-24 edge, but LSU responded with an 11-play, 73-yard march finished by Tim Ferguson's short touchdown run for a 31-27 advantage early in the fourth. The final LSU drive covered 82 yards in 12 plays, ending with McNeil's go-ahead score.

LSU won the turnover battle decisively, forcing three Miami giveaways — two Mertz fumbles recovered by Thaddeus Chadwick and Elisha Neal, plus a Kolaj Cobbins interception — while committing only one lost fumble themselves. The Tigers controlled the clock at 32:45 to 27:15 and leaned on 181 rushing yards against 103 for Miami, even as the Hurricanes outgained them through the air 318 to 200. Nussmeier was efficient at 15-of-26 for 204 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions, good for a 108.5 rating and 10th in the league in passing yards after Week 1. Mertz threw for 322 yards and two scores but the three turnovers proved costly. Chimere Dike paced all receivers with 103 yards on three catches, while Colby Lilly led Miami on the ground with 79 yards on 10 carries, ranking fifth in the PCFL in rushing yards. LSU's defense, which allowed 421 total yards (11th in the league), bent but forced the critical stops, including a fourth-down incompletion at the Miami 38 with 1:37 remaining.

The win vaults LSU to 1-0, first in the Eastern Southern and No. 1 in the power poll, while Miami drops to 0-1, fourth in the division and No. 10 in the poll. LSU averages 38 points scored and allows 27 per game through one week; Miami mirrors those marks in reverse at 27 scored and 38 allowed. Next up, LSU travels to face Arizona State (0-1), and Miami visits Washington (1-0).
aiStory.turningPoint: LSU's 12-play, 82-yard touchdown drive culminating in Rico McNeil's 2-yard run at Q4 2:24 extended a 31-27 lead to 38-27 and effectively sealed the game.
byTheNumbers: Turnover margin: LSU forced three Miami takeaways (two fumbles, one interception) while losing only one fumble.
Time of possession: LSU held the ball for 32:45 compared to Miami's 27:15, grinding the Hurricanes' defense with sustained drives in the second half.
Rushing disparity: LSU outrushed Miami 181-103, with Tim Ferguson and Rico McNeil each scoring a fourth-quarter touchdown that flipped the game.
Third-down efficiency: LSU converted 4 of 9 (44%) versus Miami's 3 of 9 (33%), extending drives that wore down the Miami front seven.

unsungHero.name: Rico McNeil
unsungHero.why: Came off the bench to deliver the go-ahead 2-yard touchdown run with 2:24 remaining, capping an 82-yard drive that turned a four-point lead into an 11-point cushion.

aiStory.headline: Arkansas Surges Past Boston College 29-20 Behind Jackson's 288 Yards
aiStory.dek: The Razorbacks claim the early power-poll top spot while the Eagles fall to 0-1 in the Eastern Atlantic.
body: With 1:32 left in the fourth quarter and Boston College trailing 20-27, Sam Leavitt was sacked by Lukas Grimes in the end zone for a safety that made it 20-29 and effectively sealed Arkansas's Week 1 victory.

Boston College struck first when Anthony Ferrucci punched in a six-yard touchdown run with 13:29 remaining in the first quarter, and Sam Leavitt found Will Graves Ill for a 17-yard strike at 11:23 of the second quarter to push the lead to 14-3 — the Eagles' largest margin at 11 points. Arkansas answered with a 16-yard touchdown pass from K.J. Jackson to Frederick Clay, then took control in the third quarter: Cruz Gibson hit a 30-yard field goal at 9:04, and Jackson connected with Mike Washington on a 47-yard touchdown pass with 10 seconds left in the period to make it 20-14. A Darius Rivas field goal pulled Boston College to 17-20 early in the fourth, but Jackson and Washington teamed for a 13-yard scoring run at the 7:00 mark, and the late safety closed the door.

The box score tells the story: Arkansas outgained Boston College 468 yards to 242, rushed for 188 against 95, and converted 42 percent of third downs to the Eagles' 33 percent. Jackson finished 19-of-34 for 288 yards and two touchdowns, vaulting him to fourth in the PCFL in passing yards, while Washington added a rushing score and the 47-yard catch. Boston College's Leavitt threw for 180 yards and a touchdown but was sacked twice in the final minute, and the Eagles' defense — ranked 14th in the league after allowing 468 yards — could not contain the Razorbacks' balanced attack. Each team lost a fumble, and Arkansas produced four offensive explosive plays of 25-plus yards.

Arkansas moves to 1-0, claims the No. 1 spot in the power poll and sits third in the Eastern Southern division behind division leader LSU, while Boston College drops to 0-1, falls to No. 10 in the poll and sits third in the Eastern Atlantic behind Texas. The Eagles host Alabama next week; the Razorbacks travel to Notre Dame.
aiStory.turningPoint: Third quarter, 0:10 — K.J. Jackson's 47-yard touchdown pass to Mike Washington gave Arkansas its first lead at 20-14.
byTheNumbers: Arkansas 468 total yards vs. Boston College 242 — the Razorbacks nearly doubled the Eagles' output and rank fifth in the PCFL in offense after Week 1.
Rushing margin 188-95 — Arkansas controlled the line of scrimmage and sustained drives, holding the ball 32:35 to Boston College's 27:25.
Third-down efficiency 42% to 33% — the Razorbacks extended possessions while the Eagles stalled, a key factor in the 20-6 scoring swing after halftime.
Each team lost one fumble — the game turned on execution, not takeaways, with Arkansas capitalizing on four offensive explosive plays of 25-plus yards.

unsungHero.name: Mike Washington
unsungHero.why: He delivered the go-ahead 47-yard touchdown catch, added a 13-yard scoring run in the fourth quarter, and chipped in 52 rushing yards to keep Arkansas's offense on schedule.

aiStory.headline: Tennessee erupts for 35 unanswered points to crush Alabama
aiStory.dek: The Volunteers seize the top power-poll spot while the Crimson Tide fall to 0-1 and last in the Eastern Atlantic.
body: With 6:19 left in the third quarter and Tennessee already up 29-17, George MacIntyre handed off to DeSean Bishop on a 16-yard touchdown run that pushed the lead to 35-17, the largest margin of the night at 18 points. Alabama answered only with a late Kingsley Ponce field goal, and the Volunteers closed out a 35-20 victory.

Alabama struck first on a 3-yard Cortez-to-Dirks touchdown pass at the end of the first quarter for a 7-0 lead. Tennessee responded with three second-quarter scores — a Justin Baker 1-yard plunge, a 76-yard MacIntyre-to-Smith strike with a successful two-point try, and another Baker 2-yard touchdown with another two-point conversion — to take a 23-10 edge before Cortez hit Terrill Fields from a yard out just before halftime to make it 23-17. The Volunteers then dominated the third quarter with Bishop touchdown runs of 4 and 16 yards, stretching the advantage to 35-17. Ponce added a 27-yard field goal in the final minute for the final margin.

The box score tells the story: Tennessee rolled up 599 total yards, leading the PCFL at 599 per game, while Alabama's defense sits last allowing 599 per game. The Volunteers rushed for 155 yards and passed for 444, with MacIntyre throwing for 447 yards — tops in the league — and Travis Smith hauling in 10 catches for 242 yards, also the league best. Alabama managed only 58 rushing yards and converted just 5 of 15 third downs; Cortez threw for 303 yards and two scores, and Fields posted 139 receiving yards, second in the PCFL. Tennessee's lone turnover, a MacIntyre interception by Marv Quirk, came too late to change the outcome, while Alabama's only giveaway — a Keith Adams Jr. fumble recovered by Mariyon Dye — helped fuel the Volunteers' surge.

Tennessee moves to 1-0, claims the No. 1 power-poll ranking and sits second in the Eastern Southern behind division leader LSU. Alabama drops to 0-1, falls to No. 10 in the poll and occupies the Eastern Atlantic cellar behind Texas. The Volunteers travel to Penn State (1-0) next week; the Crimson Tide visit Boston College (0-1) looking for their first win.
aiStory.turningPoint: Tennessee's 76-yard MacIntyre-to-Smith touchdown pass at 7:29 of the second quarter, followed by a successful two-point try, flipped a 7-7 tie into a 15-7 lead the Volunteers never relinquished.
byTheNumbers: Tennessee 599 total yards (No. 1 PCFL) vs. Alabama 348 (No. 13) — a 251-yard gap that decided the game.
Volunteers 155 rushing yards on 34 carries (4.6 avg) with two Bishop touchdowns; Crimson Tide 58 yards on 18 carries (3.2 avg).
MacIntyre 447 passing yards (league leader) and Smith 242 receiving yards (league leader) on 10 catches.
Alabama 5-of-15 on third down (33%); Tennessee 5-of-11 (45%) — the Volunteers sustained drives, the Tide stalled.

unsungHero.name: DeSean Bishop
unsungHero.why: Rushed 12 times for 60 yards and two third-quarter touchdowns that blew the game open, ranking ninth in the PCFL in rushing yards after one week.

aiStory.headline: Sayin throws four touchdowns as Ohio State rolls past Michigan 42-19
aiStory.dek: The Buckeyes open the season atop the power poll and the Western Central race while the Wolverines fall to 0-1.
body: With 2:47 left in the fourth quarter and Ohio State leading 42-19, Michigan faced fourth and just over one at the Buckeyes' 42. Chip Gabriel handed to Calvin Wendtland, who was swallowed by Payton Pierce for a loss of almost a yard, turning the ball over on downs and letting Ohio State bleed the final seconds.

Ohio State struck first and never trailed. Julian Sayin hit Devin McCuin for a short touchdown at 9:59 of the first quarter, then found Quinshon Judkins on a 24-yard scoring run at 3:57 for a 14-0 lead. Sayin added a three-yard strike to Mason Williams early in the second to make it 21-0. Michigan answered with a 75-yard drive capped by Eric Brock's three-yard run at 8:04, but Sayin orchestrated a 16-play, 74-yard march ending with a nine-yard pass to Bryson Rogers at 0:40 for a 28-7 halftime edge. Herbie Swanson hit field goals of 25 and 29 yards in the third to pull Michigan to 13-28, but Judkins punched in from three yards at 0:29 to restore a 22-point margin. Gabriel connected with Jakob Salas on a two-yard score at 13:02 of the fourth, and Sayin's fourth touchdown pass — two yards to Brandon Inniss at 9:19 — sealed the 42-19 final.

The numbers tell the story: Ohio State outgained Michigan 455-295, rushed for 236 yards to 98, and converted 9 of 11 third downs while the Wolverines managed just 5 of 11. Sayin completed 23 of 32 for 226 yards and four touchdowns with no interceptions, adding 56 rushing yards to claim Player of the Game honors; his 226 passing yards rank ninth in the PCFL early on. CJ Donaldson averaged 8.3 yards on 10 carries for 83 yards, fourth in the league. Michigan turned it over twice — a Tommie Browne interception by Earl Little at the end of the first half and a lost fumble — while Ohio State committed none. The Buckeyes held the ball for 34:20, dominating time of possession and keeping the Wolverines' offense off the field.

Ohio State moves to 1-0, claims the No. 1 spot in the power poll and sits second in the Western Central behind division leader Notre Dame with a W1 streak. Michigan drops to 0-1, falls to No. 10 in the poll and sits fourth in the division with an L1 streak. The Wolverines host UCLA (0-1) next week, while the Buckeyes travel to face Texas (1-0) in a matchup of unbeatens.
aiStory.turningPoint: Julian Sayin's nine-yard touchdown pass to Bryson Rogers with 40 seconds left in the first half extended Ohio State's lead to 28-7 and effectively put the game out of reach.
byTheNumbers: Ohio State converted 82% of third downs (9/11) versus Michigan's 45% (5/11), sustaining drives and controlling the clock.
The Buckeyes rushed for 236 yards while the Wolverines managed just 98 yards on the ground.
Michigan committed two turnovers (one interception, one lost fumble) to Ohio State's zero, a decisive margin in a 23-point game.
Julian Sayin's four touchdown passes and zero interceptions produced a 131 passer rating, the foundation of Ohio State's offensive explosion.

unsungHero.name: Quinshon Judkins
unsungHero.why: He scored two touchdowns — a 24-yard run in the first quarter and a three-yard plunge in the third — providing the ground complement that made Sayin's passing attack even more dangerous.

story.headline: Notre Dame pulls away from UCLA, 45-28

Notre Dame outgained UCLA 477 yards to 359 and controlled the clock for 38:13 compared to the Bruins' 21:47; UCLA answered with three touchdown passes from Iamaleava but went 0-for-2 on fourth down while Notre Dame converted 2 of 4.

Carr's 346 passing yards rank second in the PCFL behind only Geor MacIntyre's 447 for Tennessee, and his four touchdowns paced an offense that converted 60 percent of third downs; Price added 78 rushing yards and a touchdown on 17 carries to sit sixth in the league in rushing, while the Notre Dame defense held UCLA to 77 yards on the ground. Iamaleava threw for 282 yards and three scores but managed just 34 rushing yards, and the Bruins committed two penalties for 10 yards with one fumble lost.

Notre Dame moves to 1-0, claims the Western Central lead and sits atop the power poll at No. 1, while UCLA drops to 0-1, falls to No. 10 and trails division-leading USC in the Western Pacific; the Fighting Irish host Arkansas next week and the Bruins travel to Michigan.

aiStory.headline: Williams Jr. fuels Washington past Michigan State 25-18
aiStory.dek: Washington opens 1-0 atop the power poll while Michigan State drops to 0-1 and last in the Western Central.
body: Fourth quarter, 2:44 remaining, Washington ball at its own 37, second-and-4, clinging to a 25-18 lead. Demond Williams Jr. hands to Jordan Washington for three yards, then five on third-and-short, then Bonner Jr. rips off ten and four more to grind out first downs and bleed the clock. The Huskies kneel it out at the Michigan State 45 with 47 seconds left, sealing a 25-18 win.

Washington struck first, capping a 10-play, 80-yard opening drive with Bonner Jr.'s short touchdown run and a successful two-point try at 1:54 of the first quarter for an 8-0 edge. A 44-yard strike to Kade Eldridge set up a nine-yard touchdown catch by Justice Williams at 12:07 of the second, and a Glass fumble recovered by Rahshawn Clark at the Michigan State 30 led to a 38-yard Luke Dunne field goal and an 18-0 Washington lead at 8:07. Michigan State answered with a 78-yard drive finished by Arnold Glass finding George Sater from seven yards at 2:00, then a 41-yard Keith Rocha field goal at 4:43 of the third cut it to 18-10. Williams Jr. hit Eldridge for a one-yard score on the first play of the fourth to make it 25-10, and Glass connected with Jason Walsh on a four-yard touchdown with a two-point conversion at 10:54 to pull within seven, but the Huskies' final drive iced it.

The box score tells the story: Washington outgained Michigan State 367-215, led by Williams Jr.'s 265 passing yards, two passing scores and 91 rushing yards with a touchdown — good for Player of the Game honors. The Huskies converted 55 percent of third downs to Michigan State's 43 percent, and the lone turnover that mattered was Glass's second-quarter fumble that set up Dunne's field goal; Michigan State's only takeaway came on a muffed punt return at 13:22 of the fourth but produced no points. Bonner Jr. added 91 rushing yards and a score on eight carries, while Justice Williams paced Washington receivers with five catches for 95 yards, placing him third in the PCFL in receiving yards after Week 1. For Michigan State, Glass threw for 144 yards and two touchdowns with a 104.6 rating, 12th in the league in passing yards, and Toi Bernard broke a 31-yard run, but the Spartans managed just 97 rushing yards and 14 first downs.

Washington moves to 1-0, jumps to No. 1 in the power poll and sits second in the Western Pacific behind division leader USC at 1-0. Michigan State falls to 0-1, drops to No. 10 in the poll and occupies the Western Central cellar while Notre Dame leads the division. Next week the Spartans travel to face USC (1-0), while Washington returns home to host Miami (0-1).
aiStory.turningPoint: Glass's fumble at the Michigan State 30 with 9:05 left in the second quarter, recovered by Clark, set up Dunne's 38-yard field goal that pushed Washington's lead to 18-0.

Williams Jr. 265 passing yards, 91 rushing yards, three total touchdowns — the only player in Week 1 with 250+ passing and 90+ rushing.

story.headline: USC outlasts Colorado in 27-21 battle
body: USC found just enough in a 27-21 win over Colorado in Week 1 PCFL action, with Miller Moss earning Player of the Game honors after going for 29 of 42 for 276 yards and 3 TDs.
The Trojans outgained Colorado 424–358 in total offense, including 161 yards on the ground. Colorado kept fighting, managing 358 total yards on the night.
Up next, USC hosts Michigan State in Week 2.

aiStory.headline: Moss, USC Ground Game Close Out Colorado in Fourth Quarter
aiStory.dek: USC opens at 1-0 atop the Western Pacific while Colorado drops to 0-1 and faces Georgia next.
body: USC faced third-and-2 at the Colorado 20 with 45 seconds left and a 27-21 lead when Miller Moss handed to Woody Marks, who surged four yards for the first down that let the Trojans kneel out the clock and seal the win.

Colorado struck first on a 15-yard strike from Roger Anderson to Sam Hart at 12:53 of the first quarter, but USC answered with a 13-play, 80-yard drive capped by Moss finding Milo Beard for a one-yard score at 1:32. A Denis Lynch field goal made it 10-7 at the half. Moss hit Beard again from three yards at 6:16 of the third to push the lead to 17-7, then Anderson found Matthew Golden from three yards at 0:51 to pull Colorado within three. Moss connected with Kyle Ford for a four-yard touchdown at 11:06 of the fourth, Lynch added a 49-yard field goal at 6:05 for a 27-14 cushion, and Anderson hit Golden again from eight yards at 3:20 to set the final margin.

USC controlled the line of scrimmage with 161 rushing yards to Colorado's 56 and converted 11 of 17 third downs compared to 6 of 12 for the Buffaloes, a disparity that fueled a 35:18 to 24:42 time-of-possession edge. Moss threw for 276 yards and three touchdowns without an interception, posting a 110.8 rating that ranks sixth in the PCFL, while Carter Myers added 86 yards on 12 carries to sit third in the league in rushing. Anderson threw for 312 yards and three scores but lost a fumble and threw an interception, and Colorado's lone explosive play after halftime was a 41-yard catch by Hart that came too late to change the outcome.

The victory lifts USC to 1-0, keeps them atop the power poll at No. 1 and extends their division lead in the Western Pacific, while Colorado falls to 0-1, sits third in the Western Central behind Notre Dame, and drops to No. 10 in the poll. The Buffaloes host Georgia next week, and the Trojans welcome Michigan State, both opponents also 0-1 after the opening weekend.

story.headline: Penn State pulls away from Arizona State, 34-16
body: Penn State asserted control when it mattered in a 34-16 win over Arizona State in Week 1 PCFL action, with Reggie Brennan earning Player of the Game honors after going for 7 catches for 83 yards and 2 TDs.
The Nittany Lions outgained Arizona State 502–332 in total offense, including 150 yards on the ground. Arizona State kept fighting, managing 332 total yards on the night.
Up next, Penn State hosts Tennessee in Week 2.

aiStory.headline: Penn State pulls away late, drops 34 on Arizona State
aiStory.dek: The Nittany Lions open as the new power-poll No. 1 while the Sun Devils fall to 0-1 in the Western Pacific.
body: With 1:08 left in the fourth quarter and Penn State leading 27-16, Myers handed off to Amiel Davis on third-and-goal from the 2; Davis pushed across for the touchdown and Joseph's extra point made it 34-16, the largest lead of the night at 18 points.

Penn State struck first with a pair of Joseph field goals — 44 yards at 13:18 and 29 yards at 5:44 of the first quarter — then Myers found Brennan for a 16-yard touchdown at 2:40 to make it 13-0. Arizona State answered with Boyle's 38-yard field goal at 12:05 of the second, but Penn State drove 76 yards in 11 plays and Myers hit Brennan again, this time from 11 yards, for a 20-3 edge at 2:42. Thomas connected with Bidwell on a 10-yard score with 1:17 left in the half to cut it to 20-10. The third quarter belonged to Penn State: a 90-yard march capped by Vaughn's one-yard plunge at 5:59 pushed the lead to 27-10. Boyle added field goals of 24 and 39 yards in the fourth to draw Arizona State within 27-16, but the final Davis touchdown and a 16-play, 72-yard drive that consumed 7:17 put the game away.

The numbers tell the story: Penn State outgained Arizona State 502 yards to 332, dominated third down at 65 percent to 33 percent, and held a 150-43 edge in rushing yards. Myers threw for 367 yards and two scores on 23-of-38 passing, while Thomas completed 26 of 56 for 293 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Brennan's seven catches for 83 yards and two touchdowns earned Player of the Game honors; Clifford added 93 yards on four receptions and a 57-yard punt return that flipped field position. Arizona State's defense allowed 502 yards, ranking 17th of 18 in the league, while Penn State's unit sits fifth after holding the Sun Devils to 332.

Penn State moves to 1-0, claims the top spot in the power poll and sits second in the Eastern Atlantic behind division leader Texas with a W1 streak. Arizona State drops to 0-1, falls to fourth in the Western Pacific behind USC and sits 10th in the poll with an L1 streak. Next week the Sun Devils host LSU (1-0) while Penn State welcomes Tennessee (1-0) in a matchup of unbeatens.
aiStory.turningPoint: Penn State's 16-play, 72-yard drive culminating in Amiel Davis's two-yard touchdown run at Q4 1:08 extended the lead to 18 points and sealed the victory.
byTheNumbers: Third-down conversion rate: Penn State 11-of-17 (65%) vs. Arizona State 5-of-15 (33%) — the Nittany Lions sustained drives while the Sun Devils stalled.
Rushing disparity: Penn State 150 yards vs. Arizona State 43 yards — the Nittany Lions controlled tempo and clock on the ground.

Explosive plays: Penn State produced five gains of 25-plus yards, including Clifford's 57-yard punt return, a 42-yard strike to Evans, a 32-yard catch by Clifford, a 29-yard gain by Tyler and a 28-yard reception by Clifford; Arizona State managed one, a 37-yard catch by Johnson late in the fourth.
Turnover margin: each team threw one interception; Arizona State's Trey McNutt picked off Myers at Q1 9:18, and Penn State's Dominic Hooper intercepted Thomas at Q1 3:57.

unsungHero.name: Liam Clifford
unsungHero.why: Four catches for 93 yards and a 57-yard punt return that set up the third-quarter touchdown drive gave Penn State two critical field-position swings.

weeklyWrap.headline: Top Five Hold Firm as Week One Delivers Blowouts and Upsets
weeklyWrap.subhead: The power poll quintet went a combined 5-0 while Tennessee and Arkansas announced themselves with road statement wins.
weeklyWrap.lead: Week One produced zero movement in the top five of the power poll, but the games themselves were anything but quiet. Two of the five ranked teams won by 18 points or more, while Tennessee and Arkansas flipped scripts on the road to open the season with signature victories.

segments.title: Ohio State Rolls Over Michigan in Rivalry Rout
segments.body: Ohio State led 14-0 after one quarter and 42-7 at the half, never trailing en route to a 42-19 demolition. The Buckeyes forced one turnover and built a 23-point lead, sending an early message that the gap in this rivalry remains wide.

segments.title: Tennessee Stuns Alabama in Knoxville
segments.body: Alabama struck first with a 7-0 lead, but Tennessee erupted for 23 points in the second quarter to cut the halftime deficit to 24-23. The Volunteers forced two turnovers and pushed the margin to 18 by the third quarter en route to a 35-20 statement win.

segments.title: Arkansas Rallies Past Boston College on the Road
segments.body: Boston College led by 8 points at halftime before Arkansas flipped the script. The Razorbacks outscored the Eagles 19-6 over the final two quarters, seizing a 29-20 win with the game's only lead change coming in the second half.

segments.title: Washington and Penn State Smother Season Openers
segments.body: Both top-five teams never trailed. Washington forced two Michigan State turnovers and led by 18 at its peak in a 25-18 win. Penn State forced two Arizona State turnovers, led by 18, and cruised 34-16 to keep the defensive tone set for the conference frontrunners.

segments.title: LSU Outlasts Miami in Bayou Track Meet
segments.body: Three lead changes and a tied first quarter gave way to a 38-27 LSU victory. The Tigers grabbed an 11-point fourth-quarter lead and forced three total turnovers to survive a 65-point affair that felt like a playoff preview in September.

weeklyWrap.closer: Week Two will test whether Tennessee and Arkansas can sustain their momentum and if the top five can keep the separation intact.
